messages:
melissa: Quick check  we just hired someone starting 7/02 during a short launch blackout. How do we handle PTO accrual, year-end carryover eligibility, and the small sick-day top-up pool for hires who join during blackouts?
jordan: Accruals are pro-rated from hire date as usual. Carryover eligibility is based on being employed on Dec 31, not on whether you started in a blackout. Which blackout dates are we using this cycle?
melissa: This cycle product put a 6/287/05 no-PTO window for the launch. The new hire starts 7/02, so theyre inside it. Managers worry they'll lose carryover or be denied sick top-ups.
samir: Policy excerpt from HR policy (copied):
hr-bot: ```
Carryover: Employees on payroll as of 12/31 are eligible to carry unused PTO to the next year up to the published cap. Accruals: PTO accrues pro-rata starting the employee's hire date; partial pay periods are pro-rated. Blackout windows restrict scheduled time off but do not automatically change eligibility for accrual or carryover. Sick top-ups: a small discretionary pool exists for critical hires; grants are by manager request and require People Ops approval.
```
peter: Practically: accrual = pro-rated from 7/02 (we do partial pay-period math). Carryover = unaffected unless theyre not on payroll 12/31. Sick top-up = manager should file a one-off request; last year we approved a handful automatically for launch-critical roles but that was an ad-hoc decision.
melissa: Could we standardize the auto-grant for hires who onboard during an operational blackout? Managers ask for consistency.
samir: We can, but need to add criteria (role criticality, duration in blackout, justification) and a short workflow so payroll can tag the grant. Suggest we add a checkbox to the hiring checklist: "Auto sick-top-up eligible? (Y/N)" and require manager notes.
peter: I'll update the hire-runbook and the hiring checklist. Also will add a note to payroll: if checkbox is checked and People Ops approved, apply a one-time 6-day sick top-up in the next pay cycle.
melissa: Awesome. I'll draft a blurb for the hiring managers: "Joining during a short PTO blackout does not remove carryover eligibility; accruals are pro-rated; managers must request sick-day top-ups unless an explicit checkbox is set at hire." Will share link when done. :+1:
samir: Ping me on the draft. If we decide to make it auto by default for launch cohorts, we'll need legal sign-off and a payroll tag.
melissa: Draft posted -> https://redwood.internal/people-ops/faq/onboarding-pto-blackouts (will update). Closing the loop, thanks everyone.
